The latest published `@secretlint/formatter@13.1.0` still restricts these dependencies to older major versions:

| Dependency | Published range | Current stable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| chalk | ^5.6.2 | 6.0.1 |

Minimal range reproduction (no stress input needed):

```sh
npm view @secretlint/formatter@13.1.0 dependencies --json
```

Would you consider supporting the current majors in a release with an appropriate Node engine floor? A candidate dependency change is:

```json
{
  "chalk": "^6.0.1"
}
```

Downstream evidence: https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/31 uses exact root overrides with Node 26.13.1. Its `scripts/test_secretlint.mjs` checks detection, every console formatter, YAML loading/error handling, JSON code frames, package/license normalization and schema URI resolution. The resulting scanner lock has 76 packages, all matching registry latest, with zero project audit findings. This is a support/range request, not a claim of an exploitable vulnerability in the old range; those integration checks do not replace your full upstream suite or compatibility policy.

The local workaround is the root override until a supporting parent release is available. The migration notes and exact lock are retained in that PR. Where the new release requires Node 22 or changes module loading, please use a major release/engine update rather than silently excluding an existing supported runtime.
